Vía RecreActiva

Vía RecreActiva car-free Sunday

Guadalajara, Mexico · Avenida Vallarta, Juárez and Javier Mina, from La Minerva east · Open streets · Social

Vía RecreActiva is an open-streets program in Guadalajara, Mexico: streets closed to cars and open to bikes. It runs every Sunday from 8:00 am local time.

Next ride Sun, Oct 4, 8:00 AM CST

How we know

NNC (Sept 13, 2026) says the Vía RecreActiva, 22 years old that day, closes streets to traffic every Sunday; El Informador (Aug 16, 2026) gives the hours as 8:00 am to 2:00 pm on Sundays and official holidays (fetched Oct 1, 2026). The program's own site answers 403 to bots.

Last seen happening Sep 13, 2026.

For visitors

Free, no sign-up. Water stations, volunteer guides and traffic marshals at the crossings that stay open to cars.

First time on this ride? Here’s the drill
Bring
a helmet, water, a spare tube or patch kit, a way to pay for the stop.
Arrive
Ten or fifteen minutes before 8:00 am. Tell whoever's leading that you're new.
Pace
Pace isn't posted. Ask the host before you go, or say you're new when you arrive.
Check
Check the links below the day of for cancellations and weather calls.

About the Vía RecreActiva group ride

Guadalajara's car-free Sunday. Over 30 km of main avenues close to cars every Sunday morning across four municipalities. Ride it end to end or use it to cross the city without traffic.
